subject.name: Palomar XE325 nine simultaneous transient candidates
subject.field_description: nine point-like transient candidates within approximately 10 x 10 arcmin on a red-sensitive Palomar survey exposure

purpose: Preserve the distinction between people who have observed the physical/digital traces of the XE325 candidates and any future claim of direct naked-eye observation of a similar phenomenon.

observer_classes.finding: Nine candidate point sources were reported on the digitized red POSS-I plate from 12 April 1950. They are absent from the blue exposure roughly 30 minutes earlier, from a red plate obtained six days later, and from later/deeper surveys at the same positions.

source.title: Exploring nine simultaneously occurring transients on April 12th 1950

observer_classes.epistemic_note: This establishes the reported transient pattern in survey digitizations, not its physical origin.

observer_classes.finding: The authors visually inspected a locally held POSSI glass copy plate with microscope assistance and confirmed nine point-like detections at the reported positions.
observer_classes.interpretation_by_observers: They found the images unusually concentrated/sharp compared with typical stellar images and argued that the putative transients are likely spurious photographic-emulsion/copying artefacts.

source.title: On the nature of apparent transient sources on the National Geographic Society-Palomar Observatory Sky Survey glass copy plates

observer_classes.epistemic_note: This is evidence that the features are present on a physical glass copy and are not merely pixels invented by one digital scan. It does not establish that the features were light from the sky; the same study favors an emulsion/copy artefact explanation.

observer_classes.finding: Microscopy-based assessment registered candidate features on original glass-plate material together with an independent copy plate and found reproducibility across different representations, disfavoring a simple digitization-artifact origin.
observer_classes.limitation: Microscopy of individual point-like features cannot by itself distinguish a real short-duration optical flash from an intrinsic photographic-emulsion defect because both can produce qualitatively similar signatures.

source.title: Microscopy assessment of two multiple-transient candidates

observer_classes.epistemic_note: The simple DIGITAL_SCAN_ONLY hypothesis is weakened. The origin of the physical features remains unresolved.

future_eyewitness_firewall.rule: A person's report of occasionally seeing brief star-like flashes in the sky must be stored as an independent eyewitness stream and must not be identified with XE325 solely from phenomenological similarity.
minimum_bridge_for_comparison: azimuth and altitude or calibrated sky coordinates
independent simultaneous camera or second observer if available
checks against aircraft, satellites, meteors, atmospheric scintillation and known astronomical transients
future_eyewitness_firewall.stronger_gate: A synchronized independent instrumental detection consistent in time and sky position is required before treating an eyewitness event as a candidate member of the same physical class as an archival Palomar event.

canonical_summary_ru: Есть несколько разных классов людей, которые увидели следы XE325: команда Villarroel/VASCO обнаружила девять объектов в цифровых данных; Hambly и Blair независимо подтвердили девять точечных детекций при визуальном микроскопическом осмотре физической стеклянной копии, хотя интерпретировали их как вероятные артефакты эмульсии/копирования; Yang и Villarroel в 2026 году применили микроскопию к оригинальному материалу и независимой копии, ослабив гипотезу простого цифрового артефакта, но не разрешив развилку между реальной короткой вспышкой и дефектом эмульсии.

verdict.what_is_established: The candidate marks have existence beyond a single digitized image representation.
verdict.what_is_not_established: Their astrophysical or artificial sky origin, and any identity with future naked-eye reports.
verdict.next_best_test: synchronized multi-station imaging of future short-duration point-like flashes plus population-level archival microscopy/statistics
